Show the numbers of the manuscript, one block at a time

Source: R/blocks.R
show_blocks.Rd

show_blocks() prints the index of the blocks of the project, and show_block() prints one page of one block. They are for a screen whose numbers leave a server only as a screenshot.

Usage

show_blocks(version = NULL, home = NULL)

show_block(k, page = 1, rows = 35, version = NULL, home = NULL)

Arguments

version

The version, for example "v01". The default NULL is the version of the last initialize_project() in this R session.

home

The project folder. The default NULL is the folder of the last initialize_project() in this R session.

k

The block, by its number in blocks or by its name.

page

The page of the block, a whole number from 1.

rows

The rows of one page, a whole number from 1. The default 35 fits one screenshot.

Value

show_blocks(): invisibly, a data.frame with the columns block, name, rows, pages and error. show_block(): invisibly, the whole value of the block function.

Details

The project declares the blocks in its functions folder, as one object blocks. It is a named list of functions of results, in the order of the manuscript. The name of a block is its place in the manuscript, for example "Table 1" or "Results para 1: exclusions". Each function gets the real results as read_results() returns them. It returns a data.frame, or a character vector that prints as one line for each element. The function formats the numbers for the manuscript, and show_block() prints the table as the function returns it.

blocks <- list(
  "Table 1" = function(results) results$table1,
  "Results para 1: exclusions" = function(results) results$exclusions
)

Put blocks in the file <version>_functions/blocks.R, and nowhere else. pbn leaves that file out of manifest$source_md5, so a change of a block does not make the results stale. The rule blocks_list of check_project() fails a use of a name of that file in the other code, because the run then depends on it.

A block MAY run where the packages of the run script are missing. Examples are the console after initialize_project() and the new R session of check_one_file(). show_block() attaches no package. So a block function MUST name the package of each function that it calls, for example data.table::data.table(). When R does not find a function, the error says so.

The results include the kinds of gitexclude, so a block MAY show rows for each person, for example to find a fault. What a person copies or screenshots from the screen is the responsibility of that person.

Both functions need initialize_project() in this R session, because the blocks come from the functions folder that it sourced. Without it they stop. They read the real results from the disk at each call, with read_results(). So they work in the project folder, and on a server after the file of to_one_file(). They stop where read_results() stops. So they also stop on real results whose manifest$failed_fake_checks names a fake scenario with a failed assertion.

show_blocks() calls each block function once. For each block, it prints the number, the name, the rows and the pages. For a function that stops, it prints the error in the place of the rows, and goes on.

show_block() prints these lines:

  1. the number and the name of the block,

  2. the page, for example page 2 of 4, rows 36 to 70 of 140,

  3. the rows of the page.

Real results MAY come from fake real data, see fake_real_data of initialize_project(). Then show_block() prints the line FAKE REAL DATA between the first two lines. show_blocks() prints it under its first line.

It stops on a block function that stops, and the error names the block. During the call, the option width is 270 and the row names are off. No option of R or of data.table cuts a row or a column, and a wide table wraps its columns. Both functions record the options before a block function runs, and set them back at the end of the call. So an option that a block function sets or adds does not stay.

See also

vignette("pbn"), section "Running on an air-gapped server".

Other one file: check_one_file(), to_one_file()
